name: Early Blight
symptoms: Dark brown to black necrotic spots with characteristic concentric rings ('bull's eye' appearance)
Symptoms usually originate on older, lower foliage and progress upward
Yellow halos (chlorosis) frequently surround maturing lesions
Severe infection causes extensive defoliation, exposing fruits to sunscald
causes: Fungal pathogen Alternaria solani surviving on infected crop residues or solanaceous weed hosts
Overhead splash irrigation dispersing fungal spores

favorableConditions.weatherFactor: Warm weather punctuated by frequent showers or heavy dew cycles

prevention: Practice 2-3 year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops (e.g. cereals, pulses)
Ensure adequate plant spacing to facilitate leaf drying and canopy airflow
Utilize drip irrigation instead of overhead sprinklers to minimize leaf wetness duration
Mulch soil beneath plants to prevent rain-splash transmission from soil
management: Prune and destroy severely infected lower leaves; burn or deeply bury debris away from field
Apply protective copper-based fungicides or bio-agents like Trichoderma viride / Pseudomonas fluorescens as per package label
Ensure balanced potassium nutrition to enhance natural plant defense mechanisms
source: ICAR-IIHR Tomato Disease Advisory & TNAU Agritech Portal

name: Late Blight
symptoms: Rapidly enlarging water-soaked, irregular pale green lesions on leaves
Lesions turn dark brown to purplish-black with fuzzy white fungal growth on undersides in moist mornings
Entire vines can collapse and wither within 3 to 7 days under favorable conditions
Fruit develops firm, greasy, olive-brown sunken blotches
causes: Oomycete Phytophthora infestans wind-borne sporangia
Prolonged cool, saturated foliage

favorableConditions.humidity: Above 90% (Extended fog, cloudy days, prolonged drizzle)
favorableConditions.weatherFactor: Cool foggy mornings followed by humid overcast afternoons

prevention: Plant certified disease-free transplants or resistant hybrids
Avoid poorly drained waterlogged soils
Strictly avoid overhead irrigation during cool humid spells
management: Immediate removal and destruction of infected vines to stop rapid spore dispersal
Apply approved protective or systemic fungicides strictly under agricultural extension guidance
Maintain field sanitation and consult local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) for regional spray alert schedules

name: Tomato Leaf Curl
symptoms: Upward and inward curling, puckering, and crinkling of leaves
Severe stunting of young shoots, shortened internodes, bushy appearance
Yellowing (chlorosis) of interveinal leaf areas with thick, leathery leaf texture
Flower abortion and dramatically reduced fruit set
causes: Transmitted persistently by the whitefly vector (Bemisia tabaci)
Continuous cultivation of solanaceous crops supporting high vector populations

favorableConditions.humidity: Low to moderate humidity with dry sunny spells
favorableConditions.weatherFactor: High temperatures favoring explosive whitefly multiplication

prevention: Use nylon insect-proof net (40-50 mesh) in nurseries for 25-30 days prior to transplanting
Install yellow sticky traps (15-20 traps/acre) to monitor and mass-trap whitefly vectors
Grow border crops like maize, sorghum, or pearl millet (2-3 rows) as physical vector barriers
management: Rogue out and destroy infected viral plants during early vegetative stages
Spray 5% neem seed kernel extract (NSKE) or approved bio-pesticides to suppress vector nymphs
Consult KVK or local extension officer for IPM-compliant vector control thresholds

name: Rice Blast
symptoms: Spindle-shaped or eye-shaped lesions with grayish-white centers and brownish-red margins on leaves
Lesions coalesce, causing entire leaf blades to dry and present a scorched/blighted appearance
Neck blast: Blackish rotting of the panicle base node resulting in unfilled, completely white or broken heads
causes: Airborne conidia of Magnaporthe oryzae
Excessive and unbalanced application of nitrogenous fertilizers
Water stress or drought spells followed by heavy rains

favorableConditions.humidity: Above 90% with dew deposit duration exceeding 10 hours
favorableConditions.weatherFactor: Intermittent drizzle, overcast conditions, cool nights

prevention: Cultivate blast-resistant rice cultivars recommended for the agro-climatic zone
Apply balanced NPK fertilizers; split nitrogen into 3-4 doses rather than single heavy dressings
Seed treatment with bio-agent Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/kg seed
management: Avoid stagnant nitrogenous water runoffs between plots
Foliar spray of recommended fungicides at early tillering and panicle emergence if disease score exceeds economic threshold
Follow advisory notices issued by the Directorate of Rice Research
source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR), Hyderabad

name: Sheath Blight
symptoms: Oval or elliptical greenish-grey water-soaked spots on leaf sheaths near water line
Spots enlarge with irregular bands of brown borders resembling snake-skin pattern
Infection ascends up the sheath to flag leaf, causing lodging and empty grain heads
causes: Soil-borne sclerotia floating on floodwater contacting rice sheaths
High plant density and dense vegetative canopies

favorableConditions.weatherFactor: High ambient temperature with dense canopy canopy humidity

prevention: Optimum planting density (do not overcrowd seedlings)
Apply potassium fertilizers in split doses to strengthen stem cell walls
Drain standing water intermittently to reduce micro-humidity in canopy
management: Apply bio-control formulation of Trichoderma harzianum to soil/canopy
Spray recommended sheath protection fungicides at early symptom stage based on KVK advisory
Remove weeds from bunds that act as alternate host reservoirs

name: Bacterial Blight / Angular Leaf Spot
symptoms: Small, angular, water-soaked translucent lesions bounded by leaf veins
Lesions turn dark brown to black (Angular leaf spot phase)
Elongated black lesions on petiole and stem (Blackarm phase)
Round water-soaked spots on young bolls causing premature shedding
causes: Seed-borne and debris-borne bacterium Xanthomonas
Spreading via driving rainstorms, wind, and irrigation water

favorableConditions.weatherFactor: Continuous monsoon rains accompanied by gusty winds

prevention: Acid delinting of cotton seeds before sowing
Seed treatment with approved bio-protectants
Eradicate infected stubbles and volunteer cotton seedlings post-harvest
management: Foliar spray of copper oxychloride combined with agricultural bactericide as per official university package of practices
Maintain clean cultivation and proper field drainage
source: ICAR - Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR)

name: Bollworm Complex Damage
scientificName: Helicoverpa armigera / Earias spp. / Pectinophora gossypiella
symptoms: Bored holes on squares and developing bolls with visible granular larval frass (excreta)
Flared squares (bracts opening prematurely) and premature shedding of fruiting forms
Pink bollworm creates rosette flowers and stains internal lint
causes: Larvae hatching from eggs laid by nocturnal moths on tender leaves and flowers
Resistance buildup due to indiscriminate pesticide sprays

favorableConditions.weatherFactor: Warm humid cloudy weather during flowering and boll formation

prevention: Install pheromone traps (5 traps/acre for monitoring, 10-15 traps/acre for mass trapping)
Erect bird perches (15-20 per acre) to encourage predatory insectivorous birds
Intercrop with cowpea, pigeonpea, or marigold as trap crops
management: Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma chilonis @ 60,000/acre weekly
Spray HaNPV (Helicoverpa Nuclear Polyhedrosis Virus) or Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) formulations
Use chemical insecticides only when damage exceeds Economic Threshold Level (ETL: 1 larva/plant or 5-10% damaged bolls)

name: Soybean Rust
symptoms: Tiny, brown to reddish-brown polygonal pustules (uredinia) on underside of leaves
Pustules rupture to release tan dust-like airborne spores
Severe chlorosis, early rapid defoliation, and aborted or undersized seeds
causes: Obligate fungal pathogen Phakopsora pachyrhizi dispersing by wind over long distances

favorableConditions.humidity: Above 80% with prolonged canopy leaf wetness (> 6 hours)
favorableConditions.weatherFactor: Extended cloudy, wet spells during flowering and pod development

prevention: Early sowing of recommended tolerant varieties
Avoid excessively dense row planting to improve air circulation
Monitor lower leaves systematically from flowering stage
management: Prophylactic foliar spray of approved triazole fungicides upon first appearance of pustules in the region
Consult regional ICAR-IISR advisory bulletins for timely community-level intervention
source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Soybean Research (IISR), Indore

name: Fall Armyworm Damage
symptoms: Elongated papery feeding windows on leaves created by young neonate larvae
Extensive ragged 'shot holes' and shredded leaf whorls as larvae mature
Massive accumulation of wet yellowish-brown sawdust-like frass inside the central whorl
Boring into developing cobs and tassels
causes: High fecundity invasive pest Spodoptera frugiperda larvae feeding protected inside whorls

favorableConditions.weatherFactor: Warm conditions with intermittent rainfall fostering lush whorl growth

prevention: Deep summer ploughing to expose pupae to predatory birds and solar heat
Intercropping maize with pulses (e.g. cowpea) to disrupt egg laying
Apply sand + wood ash or neem cake mixture into central whorls of plants at 15-20 days after emergence
management: Hand-picking of egg masses and destroying early-stage larvae
Apply bio-agents Metarhizium rileyi or Beauveria bassiana @ 5g/liter
Apply whorl-directed sprays of university-approved larvicides when 10% plants show damage
source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR) & Directorate of Plant Protection

name: Chilli Anthracnose / Fruit Rot / Die-back
symptoms: Die-back: Tender twigs wither from the top downwards, turning straw-colored
Circular sunken necrotic spots on ripe red fruits with concentric rings of black acervuli
Infected fruits become bleached, dry, and shriveled; premature fruit drop
causes: Seed-borne and air-borne fungus Colletotrichum capsici
Spreads via splashing monsoon drops

favorableConditions.weatherFactor: Heavy rain showers followed by warm sunshine periods

prevention: Use disease-free seeds treated with Trichoderma viride @ 4g/kg
Collect and incinerate plant stubbles and dried infected twigs
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation during fruit development
management: Foliar spray of copper oxychloride or university-recommended fungicides at flowering and fruit formation
Ensure proper row spacing and drainage to prevent soil moisture stagnation
source: TNAU Agritech Portal & ICAR-IIHR Vegetable Division

name: Nitrogen Deficiency
symptoms: General pale green to yellow discoloration (chlorosis) beginning on older, lower leaves
V-shaped yellowing advancing from leaf tip down the midrib (especially in maize/cereals)
Stunted overall vegetative growth, thin spindly stems, and reduced tillering/branching
Premature senescence of lower foliage
causes: Insufficient soil available nitrogen
Leaching in sandy soils during torrential rains or waterlogging impeding root uptake

favorableConditions.weatherFactor: Excessive leaching rainfall or poor aeration in flooded soils

prevention: Perform periodic soil testing to determine baseline organic carbon and available nitrogen
Incorporate well-rotted farmyard manure (FYM) or compost (5-10 tonnes/hectare) prior to sowing
Practice green manuring (e.g. Dhaincha / Sunn hemp) before kharif planting
management: Foliar spray of 1% to 2% urea solution for rapid foliar recovery in standing crops
Top-dress recommended split doses of nitrogen fertilizer (Urea / CAN) matching crop growth stages
Apply bio-fertilizers like Azotobacter or Azospirillum
source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Soil Science (IISS), Bhopal

name: Potassium Deficiency
symptoms: Marginal chlorosis followed by browning and scorch ('firing') of older leaf margins
Leaf edges curl upward or downward with ragged appearance
Weak stems and culms leading to susceptibility to lodging and fungal infections
Poor grain filling and reduced fruit quality/luster
causes: Depleted soil exchangeable potassium, particularly in light sandy or acidic soils

favorableConditions.weatherFactor: Drought stress or severely leached sandy soils

prevention: Incorporate Muriate of Potash (MOP) or Sulfate of Potash as per soil test recommendations
Maintain adequate soil organic matter to enhance cation exchange capacity (CEC)
management: Foliar spray of 1% potassium nitrate (13:0:45) or sulfate of potash during peak vegetative and fruiting phases
Ensure proper irrigation as moisture facilitates potassium ion diffusion to roots
